slides.title: Ready, Steady, Go!
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 2 English, Unit 3: Ready, Steady, Go! Get ready to move! In this unit you learn the names of the parts of your body, and lots of action words such as hop, jump, clap and wave. You follow movement instructions and then give commands of your own. You also learn how to stay healthy and strong by moving every day, eating good food, drinking water and sleeping well. By the end you can say what someone is doing right now, just like Amal and her friends in this unit's story, “The Big Race”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Identify and name different parts of your body.
Understand and use action words about movement.
Follow simple movement instructions in English.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to identify and name different parts of your body. You will also understand and use action words about movement. You will also follow simple movement instructions in English. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: keep, boot, cool, cook, pull, push. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes A Poem: “Reach for the Sky!” and Healthy and Strong. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Giving Commands (Imperatives)
bullets: A command tells someone what to do. We use commands to give movement instructions in a game, in an exercise or at a race. Learning commands helps you...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Giving Commands (Imperatives). A command tells someone what to do. We use commands to give movement instructions in a game, in an exercise or at a race. Learning commands helps you follow your teacher and lead an action game yourself. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Naming Body Parts. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
